_note: CampScene lines (their own production voices). {place}, {purpose}, {km}, {day}, {ford}, {food} are filled from the journey record; lines whose keys are missing are skipped. Fireside talk picks topics from what really happened that day.

choose_site: Here. Flat ground, water close by, and those big trees will keep the wind off.
This clearing's good - we can hear the stream from here.
Let's stop here. I can't feel my feet anymore.
firewood: Firewood first, before it gets dark.
fire_lit: There we go... come on, little flame.
cook: Sweet potatoes again. I'm not complaining.
Hand me the pot? I'll start supper.
serve: Yours. Eat it while it's warm.
eat: Walking all day makes anything taste like a feast.
sleep_first: Wake me when it's my turn. Don't let me sleep through it.
Okay... I'll sleep first. Night, Luna.
after_encounter: My heart's still pounding. Did you see the size of it?
It ran from the fire... I didn't think anything that big could be scared.
take_watch: I'll watch now. You sleep - I couldn't sleep after that anyway.
wake_mate: Luna... it's morning. The sun's up.
Morning, sleepyhead. We've still got road ahead.
pack: Let's pack up. The road won't walk itself.
Fire's out. Everything packed? Then let's go.

agree_site: The stream will lull us to sleep.
water: The stream's just there. I'll fill the pot.
first_watch: I'll keep first watch. The moon keeps me awake anyway.
Sleep. I'll watch the dark for a while.
wake_mika: Mika... don't make a sound. Get up.
after_encounter: It didn't want us. It wanted the fire gone.
Old creatures fear fire. I think we were lucky.
sleep_now: Thank you. Don't let the fire die.
morning: Mm... already? It feels like I just closed my eyes.
Good morning... is there anything left to eat?

lines: Do you really think the {dest} has answers about {purpose_short}?
I think it has questions we haven't learned to ask yet. That's a start.
Your boots are still wet from {ford}, aren't they.
Squelch, squelch, all afternoon. Don't laugh.
The bread from {village} was the best thing I've eaten all week.
You said that about the cheese too.
We walked {km} kilometres today. My legs know every one of them.
The sky is different out here. So many more stars than at the Sanctuary.
There's no light to hide them. That's how the old astronomers saw the world.
Your shoulder still hurts from that troll, doesn't it.
